title: Inside Out
note: A Pixar film in which Joy, Sadness and other feelings share one mind. It argues that sadness has a job to do, and that feelings blend rather than take turns.

title: Lost in Translation
note: Two lonely strangers in Tokyo form a brief, unlabelled bond. A quiet film about jet-lagged disconnection and unexpected tenderness.

title: In the Mood for Love
note: Hong Kong in the 1960s: two neighbours are drawn together by what their spouses are doing. Restraint and longing, told through glances and music.

title: Spirited Away
note: Miyazaki’s story of a girl who must find courage and her own name in a spirit bathhouse. Wonder, fear and a nostalgia for childhood, all at once.

title: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
note: A couple erase each other from memory. It asks whether the pain is worth losing the love that came with it.

title: Amélie
note: A shy woman in Paris quietly arranges small joys for strangers, and slowly learns to risk her own happiness.

title: The Grand Budapest Hotel
note: Nostalgia for a vanished world, told as stories inside stories. Comedy with loss running underneath.

title: Wall-E
note: A lonely robot tends an abandoned Earth. Almost wordless, tender and hopeful.

title: Moonlight
note: Three chapters in one man’s life, growing up in Miami. Shyness, identity and tenderness, mostly unspoken.

title: Whiplash
note: A young drummer and a brutal teacher. Ambition tipping into obsession, and what it costs.

title: Paddington 2
note: A kind bear is wrongly jailed and wins people over anyway. Warmth and gratitude as a form of strength.

title: Arrival
note: A linguist tries to talk with visitors from elsewhere. A story about grief, time, and loving someone knowing you will lose them.
